classification.difficultyReason: Establish parallelism using converse angle tests, then calculate unknown angles with reasons.

content.prompt: In each diagram below, give a reason why $AB\parallel CD$. Hence, find the values of $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$.

spec.description: Triangle OCD with A on OC, B on OD and internal segment AB. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: O,A,C collinear; O,B,D collinear; angle OAB and angle OCD are 55 degrees; angle CDO is 38 degrees; angle ABO is beta.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied angles and the unknown beta appear.

answer.short: $AB\parallel CD$ because corresponding angles $\angle OAB=\angle OCD=55^\circ$. $\beta=38^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$\angle OAB=\angle OCD=55^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$ because corresponding angles are equal.

$\beta=38^\circ$ (corresponding angles, $AB\parallel CD$).

spec.description: Horizontal AB above CD with crossed transversals AD and BC meeting at V; source blue strokes become black.
spec.mathematics: BAV=45 degrees, ABV=30 degrees, CDV=45 degrees, VCD=gamma.

answer.short: $AB\parallel CD$ because alternate angles $\angle VAB=\angle VDC=45^\circ$. $\gamma=30^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$\angle VAB=\angle VDC=45^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$ because alternate angles are equal.

$\gamma=30^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CD$).

spec.description: Crossed transversals AD and BC meet at V between AB and CD; source blue strokes become black.
spec.mathematics: BAV=50 degrees, ABV=30 degrees, CDV=50 degrees, VCD=theta.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and theta appear.

answer.short: $AB\parallel CD$ because alternate angles $\angle VAB=\angle VDC=50^\circ$. $\theta=30^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$\angle VAB=\angle VDC=50^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$ because alternate angles are equal.

$\theta=30^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CD$).

spec.description: Quadrilateral ABDC with AC vertical, AB and CD horizontal and BD oblique; retain both right-angle squares.

answer.short: $AB\parallel CD$ because the co-interior angles at $A$ and $C$ total $180^\circ$. $\alpha=105^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$\angle BAC+\angle ACD=90^\circ+90^\circ=180^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$ because co-interior angles are supplementary.

$\alpha+75^\circ=180^\circ$ (co-interior angles, $AB\parallel CD$).

$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-75^\circ\\\alpha&=105^\circ\end{align*}$$
